intro: São Tomé and Príncipe is Africa's second-smallest country, two volcanic islands that were uninhabited until the Portuguese arrived.

chapters.title: Settlement
text: Portuguese sailors found the islands around 1470. Settlers brought enslaved Africans to grow sugar, and the islands became a slave-trade hub.

chapters.title: Cocoa islands
text: In the late 1800s São Tomé became one of the world's top cocoa producers, using contract workers in harsh conditions. A 1953 massacre at Batepá killed hundreds of protesters.

chapters.title: Independence
text: The islands became independent in 1975. Multi-party democracy began in 1991, and power has changed hands peacefully.

highlight.title: Peaceful
highlight.text: Elections have led to several peaceful changes of government.
